title: Mirror force-code stability across long rollouts
hypothesis: A fixed material Mirror code in an energy-derived force law preserves NVE trajectory stability as well as a functionally identical native material coefficient; a separately perturbed force field is unstable/nonconservative.
physical_object: Shared Lennard-Jones pair potential and velocity-Verlet simulator
mirror_coordinate: Fixed per-material epsilon scale code m

development.selection_metric: fixed dt 0.002 and 3000 NVE steps; no tuning beyond detecting integration failure

success_gate: Both views complete all 3000 steps with finite state and relative NVE energy drift <1e-3 in every fresh world; Mirror trajectory agrees with its native coefficient alias within 1e-10; negative control exhibits detectable energy drift or force-gradient inconsistency.
failure_gate: Catastrophic rollout, energy drift threshold exceeded, physical consistency violation, or alias fails to replay.
boundaries: Synthetic LJ NVE integrator screen only; not MatterSim/MACE MD or material stability evidence.
No NVT sampling, periodic boundary conditions, or thermodynamic ensemble claims.
Passing validates a fixed-code trajectory mechanism only, not Mirror-specific advantage.
decision: Scoped synthetic NVE stability validated; Mirror matches native coefficient alias and adds bytes/compute.
